p: On Rosh Hashanah the custom is
to eat an apple in honey,
and we say, "May it be Your will
that You renew for us a good and sweet year."
The matter of the renewal of the year
that the Shabbosos and Roshei Chodashim of the year
each have a holiness of their own,
כָּל שַׁבָּת וְכָל חוֹדֶשׁ לְפִי בְּחִינָתוֹ
every Shabbos and every month according to its aspect.
וּבְהַגִּיעַ הַיּוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
And when the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah arrives,
קְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַזְּמַנִּים עַל הַשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה
the holiness of all the holy times for the coming year,
to bestow anew an awakening of holiness in the soul,
as at the beginning of Creation.
Therefore it is called the Day of Remembrance,
"For You bring a decree of remembrance before You
for all deeds to be recalled."
And as we say in the tefillah and in the Kiddush of the day:
"And Your word, our King, is true and enduring forever";
that is, the word of Hashem
through which all creatures were created
to be renewed each and every year.
that You renew the year for us for good;
that is, that our heart be renewed in all matters
to conduct ourselves in them in the good way,
which is according to the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
following the way of the Torah,
"Say of the tzaddik that he is good."
וְצַדִּיק נִקְרָא מִי שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר אֶת דְּרָכָיו
And a tzaddik is one who guards his ways
to walk in the good and upright path
before Him, Yisbarach, in the way of the Torah,
even if he does not yet feel within himself
taste and sweetness in his engagement with holiness
so as to be joyful in his avodah,
"Tzaddikim to light, and the upright to joy,"
where at the start of the sowing
אֵינֶנּוּ יוֹדֵעַ עוֹד מַה יִּצְמַח מִזֶּה
one does not yet know what will grow from it.
But "and for the upright of heart, joy":
taste and sweetness in the avodah,
until joy is born from this in his heart.
And this is the intent of "sweet":
it is the feeling of taste and joy in the heart.
And as an allusion to this
we eat an apple in honey,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פח, א)
in line with what Chazal said (Shabbos 88a)
that Yisrael are likened to an apple:
מַה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו
just as with this apple its fruit comes before its leaves,
so too Yisrael put "we will do" before "we will hear."
that one does the aspect of good
while he does not yet feel the taste,
רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת מַה שֶּׁיִּצְטַוֶּה מֵרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
only doing what he is commanded by His will, Yisbarach,
to walk in the way of the Torah.
And "we will hear" is the feeling of taste
so that the sweetness is absorbed into his heart
with joy and with good sense and knowledge;
this is the meaning of "we will hear."
And this is the allusion of the apple
which is the aspect of "we will do," as mentioned above,
the aspect of "Say of the tzaddik that he is good."
And honey alludes to the sweetness of hearing
and understanding with good sense and knowledge,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַרְגִּישׁ הַשִּׂמְחָה בְּלִבּוֹ
through which he feels the joy in his heart,
in line with what is said (Shoftim 14:18):
And as above: "and for the upright of heart, joy."
